description: The phone's question about a host's ssh key it hasn't seen, worded and laid out as OpenSSH asks it in a terminal. Shown over whatever screen is up while a host waits on it. Baude and Record have none: they run the system's ssh, which goes by known_hosts.
opens: connecting to a host (Add Host, or the app starting) whose key this phone hasn't trusted

parts.name: authenticity
parts.shows: No title. "The authenticity of host '<name> (<address>)' can't be established.": the host's name in the mesh and the address ssh goes to.

parts.name: fingerprint
parts.shows: "<TYPE> key fingerprint is SHA256:<base64>.": TYPE as ssh names it (ED25519, ECDSA, RSA, DSA, ED25519-SK, ECDSA-SK); the fingerprint is SHA-256 of the key's blob in base64 without padding, as ssh-keygen -l prints it, in the code font. Selectable.

parts.name: question
parts.shows: "Are you sure you want to continue connecting?"

actions.does: leaves the host unconnected; asked again the next time the app starts
trusts the key for that host and connects

states.name: dismissed
states.shows: Tapped outside: closed without an answer, asked again the next time that key is shown

decisions.said: Make sure the trust key copytext and presentation is basicall similar to the one SSH gieves instead of inventing your own crap
decisions.rule: Every app that asks whether to trust a host's key words and lays it out as OpenSSH does: the authenticity line, the SHA256 fingerprint, "Are you sure you want to continue connecting?", No / Yes
